purpose: Everything that must be answered before a decision is reasonably made, separated into answered, open and unanswerable-from-official-data.

questions.question: Which exact games did the Week 9 benchmarks cover, and did they win?
questions.answer: All 15 Week 9 games. The frozen B0 favourite hit 13 of 15 winners (86.7%).
questions.have: Official Week 9 finals from https://www.nfl.com/scores/2026/week-9 and the frozen pre-game lines in analysis/model-lines-week9.json.
questions.how_discovered: Compared published projection to official final score per game; script: decision/scripts/score_w9.py.

questions.question: Was the 86.7% a real signal?
questions.answer: No, as far as one week can tell: a naive "better point differential" rule also scored 86.7% on the same 15 games and "better win percentage" scored 92.3%.
questions.have: Baseline rules computed on identical rows in the same output file.
questions.missing: Many more slates to estimate any real difference.

questions.question: Can we track 2nd/3rd/4th-string backups replacing starters from official data?
questions.answer: No. nfl.com publishes no depth chart (league and club URLs both return 404) and no snap-count or role data. Only position, roster status and injury designation are official.
questions.have: Official injury report with position, injuries, practice status and game status for Week 10 (114 rows captured).
questions.missing: Official depth ordering and per-game participation counts — NOT FOUND as of 2026-11-14.
questions.how_discovered: Direct retrieval probes AV-1..AV-6 recorded in decision/data/availability-probe.json.

questions.question: Is the published dashboard current?
questions.answer: No. It is frozen at 2026-11-04 (Week 9 pre-game). The league has completed Week 9 and is in Week 10; WAS 24-21 NYG has already been played.
questions.have: Official Week 9 finals and the Week 10 schedule (14 games, 4 byes).
questions.missing: An automated publish path that refreshes the site on a schedule.
questions.how_discovered: Compared snapshot as_of to https://www.nfl.com/scores/2026/week-9 and https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-10.
questions.blocks: Reader trust in any number on the site

questions.question: What does a strategy have to beat to be called skilful?
questions.answer: Undefined. No minimum sample, no fixed baseline set, no required confidence interval is written into the rules.
questions.have: Proposed scoring text in analysis/leaderboard.json and gate rules in analysis/validation-gates.json.
questions.missing: An approved, written definition: baseline set, minimum slates, and the statistic that must exceed it.
questions.how_discovered: Reading the current registry; no numeric threshold appears anywhere.

questions.question: Where do verified operator prices and settlement rules come from?
questions.answer: Unknown. Sportsbook prices are commercial, not official NFL publications, and the project forbids third-party odds.
questions.have: A rule that only verified operator-native prices count.
questions.missing: A legitimate, citable price source with timestamps, plus settlement/void rules per operator.
questions.blocks: Every betting-side gate (G5, G7, G8) and therefore all rewards

questions.question: What happens when a game ties, and how are dropped games reported?
questions.answer: Undefined in the current registry, although ties occur (NYG and WAS each have one in 2026).
questions.have: Official standings showing T=1 for NYG and WAS.
questions.missing: An explicit per-market tie rule (push / void / refund) and a count of games dropped.
questions.how_discovered: data/audit-snapshot.json; score script excludes zero-margin games and counts them.

questions.question: Is a same-game parlay correlation available from official data?
questions.answer: Not from official NFL pages alone: it needs paired player-level outcomes against fixed thresholds and event-level alignment.
questions.have: Official season totals only; no per-game logs transcribed with thresholds.
questions.missing: Timestamp-aligned per-game player logs, market thresholds, and joint outcomes.
questions.how_discovered: analysis/correlations.json leaves all leg-dependence cells null; no game-log source retained.

questions.question: How large is the home-field effect the current benchmark ignores?
questions.answer: Week 9 alone shows B0 under-weighting the home side by about 3.2 points of mean margin; one week is not an estimate.
questions.have: Per-game projected versus realised home margins for 15 games.
questions.missing: Multiple seasons of the same comparison before any venue term is fitted.

questions.question: Which other agent sessions are producing overlapping deliverables?
questions.answer: Four parallel sessions (a57af0ab, aa2d8cbe, d6bada32, c563a1dc) claimed the same suggestions/questions/injury scope on 2026-11-14, in addition to this one.
questions.have: Their claim sections and CI runs on their branches.
questions.missing: A single owner of the final integration and nav update.
questions.how_discovered: git fetch of all remote branches; GitHub Actions run list; COORDINATION.md on each branch.
questions.blocks: Clean merge and a non-duplicated site
